program: MSc Creative Music and Sound Design for Visual Media Scoring (listed in French as 'Master of Science in Sound Design and Music on Screen')
qualification: NOT a diplôme national de master. It is an institutional Université Côte d'Azur MSc — a diplôme d'établissement / diplôme d'université (DU). UniCA's English MSc portal states these are 'State-accredited MSc degree courses' but the French offer-of-training page describes only an 'MSc (Master of Science)' institutional degree, and Onisep indexes every UniCA international MSc under the structure 'IDEX d'Université Côte d'Azur (MSc internationaux)' with diploma pages titled 'DU ...' (e.g. onisep.fr/.../du-msc-affluencers-and-luxury, /du-science-conservation-valorisation-des-ressources-marines). Separately, UniCA's own newsroom announced 'Le grade de master reconnu pour 8 Diplômes d'établissement' — by arrêté of 17 March, the grade de master was conferred on eight named UniCA diplômes d'établissement (biobanks and complex data management; biocontrol for plant health; environmental risk management; management of aromas and perfumes sector; modeling of neural and cognitive systems; science, conservation and valorization of marine resources; data science and artificial intelligence; smart-EdTech). The music/sound MSc is NOT among those eight. VERDICT: institutional MSc, diplôme d'établissement, without diplôme national de master status and without a separately conferred grade de master.
accreditationStatus: Public university (Université Côte d'Azur) but this specific award is an institutional IDEX MSc, not a nationally accredited master mention. Grade de master NOT established for this diploma (UNVERIFIED that any later arrêté added it).
institutionType: (b/c) Public university awarding an institutional (non-national) diploma — therefore OUTSIDE the décret n°2026-385 frais différenciés regime, which applies to diplômes nationaux. UniCA sets the MSc price itself.
whatYouStudy: Composition, orchestration, sound design, creative management, artistic entrepreneurship, spatial audio and post-production on Dolby Atmos (Dolby partnership; students also receive a professional Dolby Atmos certification). Each year ends with the student's own composition performed live by the Orchestre National de Cannes. Studio facilities at Campus Georges Méliès (50 m2 sound studio, 250 m2 stage, IT room partnered with Native Instruments and iZotope).
entryRequirements: Quote: 'A bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) in the fields of music or arts, or a degree in humanities with significant experience in music'; 'A good command of English, minimum B2 level'; 'Proof of at least cycle 2 conservatory level, or foreign equivalent (play an instrument)'.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — effectively closed to this candidate. The page requires a bachelor 'in the fields of music or arts, or a degree in humanities with significant experience in music' (a BSc in Software Engineering is neither), AND 'Proof of at least cycle 2 conservatory level, or foreign equivalent (play an instrument)'. The French page also demands applicants 'present their own musical creation, demonstrate a high level of proficiency in music writing (harmony, counterpoint, orchestration,) or electronic composition, and in the use of a DAW.' Hard blocker: no conservatoire training.
portfolioSpec: Exact, quoted from the Application page: (1) 'A 2-4 min long video stating your motivation and professional project'; (2) 'Your personal audio production'; (3) 'Your own scores made on a computer (score of your audio production)'. Number of audio works not numerically specified on the page (UNVERIFIED).
auditionSpec: No live audition stated. Instead, documentary proof: 'Proof of at least cycle 2 conservatory level, or foreign equivalent (play an instrument)'. Selection is on dossier + video + audio production. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is held.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 5,500 per year. Quote from the Application page: French/European students '€300 and €5,500 per year maximum'; international students (non-EU) '€5,500 for international students'.
otherFees: CVEC (contribution vie étudiante et de campus) — UNVERIFIED whether payable on a diplôme d'établissement. Living costs in Cannes are high.
totalCostEstimate: ~EUR 11,000 tuition over 2 years, plus living costs (Cannes/Nice, budget ~EUR 900-1,200/month) => roughly EUR 33,000-40,000 for the full programme.
scholarshipName: UniCA MSc scholarships / IDEX scholarships (a 'Scholarships' and 'Sponsorship' section exists at univ-cotedazur.eu/msc-programs/tuition-fees)
scholarships: UNVERIFIED — the scholarship page content did not render; amounts and eligibility not confirmed from an official page.
languageRequirement: English B2 minimum. No French required.
englishTest: Quote: accepted tests are 'IELTS, TOEFL IBT, TOEFL ITP, TOEIC, General GRE, Cambridge English Exam (B2 First/FCE)'.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026 entry): 'mid-June; for the start of the academic year in September'. For Sept 2027 entry assume a comparable mid-June 2027 deadline (UNVERIFIED). Note: as a non-EU candidate resident in Tunisia he must go through Études en France/Campus France, whose master deadline (~15 Jan 2027) is much earlier than the programme's own June deadline — the Campus France calendar governs. Campus France Tunisie / Études en France procedure applies: platform opens 1 October 2026; master applications close approx. 15 January 2027 for Sept 2027 entry.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE: 'Opening: January each year'. Applications go through eCandidat Université Côte d'Azur; the UniCA page states non-European candidates go via the 'Études en France' platform.

qualification: Diplôme national de master (DNM), grade de master, niveau bac+5
accreditationStatus: Accredited public university master mention (Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur). Delivered by Rennes 2, arts department.
institutionType: (a) Public university — SUBJECT to the décret n°2026-385 frais différenciés regime. Décret n°2026-385 du 19 mai 2026 makes frais différenciés the default from Sept 2026: master reference rate 3941 EUR/yr for non-EU students; institutional exemptions capped at 25% of non-EU students in 2027-28. UNVERIFIED whether this institution will exempt him.
language: French. The programme states C1 written French is expected of international students.
whatYouStudy: Art-technology intersection: experimental creation, VR/AR, interactive 3D, generative visual work, aesthetics and methodology (M1). Sound/electronic content is present but as optional workshops: 'synthèse sonore et traitements du son', 'musiques expérimentales', and workshops listed as 'Synthèse sonore, musiques électroniques expérimentales, Espace et spatialisation'. This is a digital-arts master with an electronic-music strand, not a dedicated electronic music master.
entryRequirements: Bac+3 in any artistic discipline, or a technology/IT degree with demonstrated interest in the arts. Quote: 'Toutes les disciplines artistiques (université ou école d'art Bac +3) sont concernées.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — and unusually favourable to his exact profile. The programme explicitly welcomes candidates from technology/computer-science backgrounds who can demonstrate an interest in the arts, alongside candidates from all artistic disciplines. A BSc Software Engineering is an accepted entry route in principle; the arts interest must be evidenced by the dossier. (Exact French wording for the tech-route sentence UNVERIFIED beyond the programme page summary.)
portfolioSpec: Dossier, not a formal portfolio spec. Required: detailed course/curriculum documentation, diplomas and transcripts, a lettre de motivation setting out professional and study objectives, CV, and — quote — 'documents ou œuvres produits par le candidat permettant d'attester de ses compétences'. No number of works, no duration, no format specified on the page. Practical effect: he must produce SOME body of work, but the school does not dictate its size.
auditionSpec: No live audition or épreuve mentioned. Selection is sur dossier via the national platform. UNVERIFIED whether shortlisted candidates are interviewed.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as a published figure for 2027-28. Under décret n°2026-385 the master reference rate for non-EU students is EUR 3,941/yr unless Rennes 2 grants an exemption (exemptions capped at 25% of non-EU students in 2027-28). The EU/exempted national rate was EUR 250/yr for master in recent years (UNVERIFIED for 2027-28).
otherFees: CVEC (approx. EUR 105 in 2025-26, indexed annually — UNVERIFIED for 2027-28).
totalCostEstimate: If charged differentiated fees: ~EUR 4,050/yr tuition+CVEC + living in Rennes (~EUR 750-900/month) => roughly EUR 13,000-15,000/yr. If exempted: ~EUR 360/yr + living.
scholarshipName: Bourse du gouvernement français (BGF) via Ambassade de France en Tunisie; Eiffel Excellence (Campus France) — institution must nominate; Rennes 2 does not publish a dedicated international scholarship for this master (UNVERIFIED).
languageRequirement: French C1 written expected for international students. DELF/DALF or TCF normally required by Campus France.
deadline: For a Tunisian resident with a foreign diploma the route is Études en France (Campus France Tunisie), NOT monmaster.gouv.fr. Campus France Tunisie / Études en France procedure applies: platform opens 1 October 2026; master applications close approx. 15 January 2027 for Sept 2027 entry. French/EU-resident candidates use monmaster.gouv.fr (PRIOR CYCLE: national window typically late Feb to late March). Exact Rennes 2 dates for 2027 entry UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: Études en France opens 1 October 2026 for Sept 2027 entry.

institution: École supérieure d'art et de design TALM — site du Mans (TALM-Le Mans)
program: DNSEP Design, mention Design sonore (années 4 et 5)
qualification: DNSEP — Diplôme national supérieur d'expression plastique, CONFÉRANT LE GRADE DE MASTER. Not a diplôme national de master. The school's own brochure is titled 'DNSEP grade de master — Façonner le son : du sens à l'usage — DESIGN SONORE'. Footer quote: 'TALM est un établissement public sous tutelle du ministère de la Culture, délivrant des diplômes d'État.'
accreditationStatus: État diploma, Ministry of Culture tutelle. Programme built on a partnership: quote — 'La mention Design sonore résulte d'un partenariat entre l'École supérieure d'art et de design TALM, l'IRCAM, l'ENSCI - Les Ateliers et le Laboratoire d'acoustique de Le Mans Université (LAUM).'
institutionType: (b) Ministry of Culture école d'art — OUTSIDE the décret n°2026-385 frais différenciés regime (that regime governs diplômes nationaux in universities). Écoles d'art territoriales/nationales set their own droits.
durationEcts: 2 years (années 4 and 5 of the 5-year cursus), entry directly into année 4. 120 ECTS. Cohort quote: 'accessible à une dizaine de jeunes diplômé.e.s' (about ten places).
whatYouStudy: Applied sound creation across industry, urbanism/architecture, museum space, digital media, object design, art, cinema and live performance. Quote: 'Les élèves sont formé.e.s à la méthodologie de projet, à la création sonore et à la conception de dispositifs sonores au sens large. La formation aux savoirs et compétences en acoustique ainsi qu'à l'ingénierie du son, permet de traduire un projet donné en une production sonore.' Teaching team includes IRCAM researchers (Olivier Houix, coordination; Nicolas Misdariis and Patrick Susini of IRCAM's Perception et Design Sonores team as external contributors) and Roland Cahen (ENSCI sound studio). Year opens with an applied workshop answering a real industrial or institutional commission. Note the brochure positions it AGAINST narrow specialisation: 'Contrairement aux formations proposant des objectifs très spécialisés (design musical, son à l'image, jeux vidéos, etc.)...'
entryRequirements: Quote in full: 'Le.la candidat.e peut être diplômé.e d'une filière artistique ou d'électroacoustique des universités (ou être inscrit.e en licence au moment du concours - titre RNCP niveau II -) ; d'une école d'art ou de design équivalent au niveau licence (DNA ou équivalents étrangers) ; d'une école d'enseignement musical spécialisé équivalent au niveau licence (DNSPM ou équivalents étrangers), d'un DEM de composition ou électroacoustique d'un établissement musical spécialisé agréé par l'État, à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines.'
acceptsNonMusic: BORDERLINE — probably NOT on the literal wording, but the framing invites him. The listed entry diplomas are all artistic/electroacoustic/art-school/music-school; a bare BSc in Software Engineering appears only as the *supplement* ('à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique') to a DEM in composition or electroacoustics — i.e. the scientific licence alone is not an entry title. Against that, the brochure's opening sentence is deliberately wide: 'Ce DNSEP s'adresse à tout type de créat.eurs.rices sonores, designers, musicien.ne.s, composit.eurs.rices, artistes, dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter aux champs d'application très divers du design sonore.' and 'La motivation, l'ouverture d'esprit, la faculté d'adaptation à des contextes spécifiques, le potentiel à travailler en équipe sont autant d'éléments déterminants au moment du recrutement.' Practical read: a strong portfolio plus a software-engineering background is a credible commission case, but he should write to olivier.houix@talm.fr first.
portfolioSpec: EXACT, quoted from 'Pièces constitutives du dossier de candidature': (1) 'Dossier administratif'; (2) 'Curriculum vitae détaillant les acquis de formation sonore, acoustique design, pratique artistique, projets personnels'; (3) 'Une lettre de motivation argumentée sur la conception du design sonore, les domaines d'intérêt'; (4) 'Catalogue de réalisations artistiques, dessins, vidéos, musiques, photos, peinture, sculpture, etc.'; (5) 'Catalogue de réalisation sonore - 1 ou plusieurs extraits pour un total de 5 minutes maximum. Pour chaque extrait il est nécessaire de définir par écrit l'objectif artistique ou de design, la nature originelle du document et le format du fichier'; (6) 'Un projet d'échange international ou de stage qui a lieu au deuxième semestre'; (7) 'Un projet de mémoire.' NOTE: the sound portfolio is capped at FIVE MINUTES TOTAL — an unusually small and therefore achievable ask for someone with no portfolio yet.
auditionSpec: No live musical audition. Quote: 'L'entrée au DNSEP passe par la réussite à une commission qui se déroule en deux temps : - une phase d'admissibilité (un dossier) ; - une phase d'admission (un entretien).' So: dossier shortlisting, then an interview with the jury.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — TALM does not publish a per-year droits d'inscription figure for the DNSEP on a page I could reach (the 'Inscriptions' and 'Tarifs' pages found are for the cours publics, not the diplôme cursus; esad-talm.fr returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch). Écoles supérieures d'art under Ministry of Culture tutelle typically charge in the EUR 400-900/yr range and are NOT subject to the university frais différenciés. Do not assume; verify with the school.
otherFees: Concours/commission application fee UNVERIFIED. CVEC payable (~EUR 105, UNVERIFIED for 2027-28). Sound/production material costs.
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED tuition; living in Le Mans is among the cheapest in France (~EUR 600-750/month). Likely well under EUR 12,000/yr all-in if tuition is in the usual école d'art range.
scholarshipName: Bourses sur critères sociaux du ministère de la Culture (normally nationality/residence restricted); Bourse du gouvernement français (BGF) via the French Embassy in Tunisia; Eiffel (Campus France).
scholarships: UNVERIFIED for non-EU candidates at TALM.
languageRequirement: French required (teaching, jury interview, mémoire). Level not published — UNVERIFIED, but B2/C1 is the practical norm and Campus France Tunisie will require a French test.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 'Les dossiers d'inscription à la commission sont mis en ligne chaque année sur notre site internet mi-janvier. La présélection puis l'entretien avec le jury se déroulent entre début avril et mi-mai selon les années.' A 2025 commission cycle closed 13 March 2025. For Sept 2027 entry expect the dossier online mid-January 2027, closing March 2027, interviews April-May 2027. Campus France Tunisie / Études en France procedure applies to him: platform opens 1 October 2026; master applications close approx. 15 January 2027 for September 2027 entry.
applicationOpens: Mid-January each year (dossier published on esad-talm.fr).

institution: Haute école des arts du Rhin (HEAR) — Académie supérieure de musique de Strasbourg, jointly with Université de Strasbourg
program: Master professionnel « Composition et interprétation musicale » (CIM), option « Création et interprétation électroacoustique »
qualification: Diplôme national de master. Quote: the diploma is 'délivré par l'Université de Strasbourg' — HEAR co-delivers the artistic teaching, Unistra awards the DNM. This is the record that also settles Université de Strasbourg for Field A.
accreditationStatus: Accredited DNM (Université de Strasbourg) delivered in partnership with HEAR, an établissement public under Ministry of Culture tutelle.
institutionType: HYBRID: (a) the degree is a university DNM at Université de Strasbourg, so the décret n°2026-385 frais différenciés regime applies to the Unistra registration; (b) HEAR charges its own separate droits as a Ministry of Culture school. He would pay BOTH.
language: French. Quote: 'Ce cursus exige un niveau C1 de français.'
durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS (30/semester); 60 ECTS in M1 required to pass to M2.
whatYouStudy: Over 40 instrumental/vocal options; the relevant one is 'Création et interprétation électroacoustique'. HEAR's electroacoustic and real-time composition class is taught by Tom Mays. Quote on the department: the two composition classes form a department covering 'toutes les formes de musique instrumentale, vocale, mixte, électroacoustique, électronique, temps réel' and hybrid music/art forms. University side delivers 'langues appliquées à la musicologie, l'histoire et la théorie de l'interprétation'; HEAR side delivers instrumental/vocal discipline, collective practice, conducting, prise de son, arrangement. Applied didactics include electroacoustics and musical computing.
entryRequirements: Not published in detail on the pages reached — UNVERIFIED. Structurally a DNSPM (or licence de musique) plus a successful concours is the standard route; applications go through BOTH the HEAR 'plateforme de saisie Taïga' AND monmaster.gouv.fr for the Université de Strasbourg side.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED, but treat as NO in practice. This is a conservatoire-track performance/composition master with a competitive entrance examination and a C1 French requirement; nothing on the pages reached admits candidates without prior specialised musical training. No quote available admitting non-music backgrounds.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — not published on the admissions page reached. Expect a dossier plus works for the electroacoustic option.
auditionSpec: Concours d'entrée exists (an 'entrance exam' fee of EUR 60 per programme is charged, which implies épreuves). Exact épreuves for 'Création et interprétation électroacoustique' UNVERIFIED — not quoted on the pages reached.
tuitionNonEU: TWO fees. (1) HEAR droits: 'Tuition: 378 € (full rate); 0 € (scholarship holders)' for 2025-2026 — PRIOR CYCLE. (2) Université de Strasbourg droits: EUR 164 (master, 2024-2025 reference, PRIOR CYCLE), with the page noting non-EU students 'May face droits différenciés of 2,586 €'. That EUR 2,586 is the OLD (2019 regime) master differentiated rate; under décret n°2026-385 the master reference becomes EUR 3,941/yr from Sept 2026, with exemptions capped at 25% of non-EU students in 2027-28. Budget EUR 3,941 + EUR 378 unless exempted.
otherFees: Concours fee EUR 60 per programme (PRIOR CYCLE). CVEC.
totalCostEstimate: Worst case ~EUR 4,400/yr in fees + Strasbourg living (~EUR 850-1,000/month) => ~EUR 15,000-16,500/yr. Best case (exempted) ~EUR 650/yr in fees.
scholarshipName: HEAR exempts scholarship holders from its own droits ('0 € — boursiers'); Bourse du gouvernement français via the French Embassy in Tunisia; Eiffel via Unistra nomination.
scholarships: UNVERIFIED whether a Tunisian non-EU candidate can qualify for the boursier exemption (French CROUS bourses sur critères sociaux are normally residence-restricted).
languageRequirement: French C1 — explicitly required. This is a hard gate: he is French-fluent, so this is one of the few conservatoire-level programmes where language is not the obstacle.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 'Les candidatures à l'Académie supérieure de musique de Strasbourg / HEAR – Musique s'ouvrent le 06 janvier 2026.' Parallel monmaster.gouv.fr application required for the Unistra side. Campus France Tunisie / Études en France procedure applies to him: platform opens 1 October 2026; master applications close approx. 15 January 2027 for September 2027 entry. Because he holds a foreign diploma and lives in Tunisia, the Études en France route (closing ~15 Jan 2027) may supersede monmaster — confirm with both institutions.
applicationOpens: Early January (6 January in the 2026 cycle).

program: Master mention Arts, parcours « Musicologies et créations musicales contemporaines »
accreditationStatus: Accredited university master. THIS IS THE RENAMED PARCOURS: the older Lille music master parcours was 'Musique, interprétation, invention' (its URL fr-00115804 now 404s / redirects); the live catalogue entry under Master Arts carries the code MX115804 with the current title 'Musicologies et créations musicales contemporaines'. Same parcours code, new name.
institutionType: (a) Public university — SUBJECT to décret n°2026-385 frais différenciés (master reference EUR 3,941/yr; exemptions capped at 25% of non-EU students in 2027-28).
whatYouStudy: Quote: the parcours privileges 'musiques composées ou improvisées, électroacoustiques ou mixtes' as much as the relationship between contemporary creation and ethnomusicology. Approaches: composition, aesthetics, semiotics, hermeneutics, performance/improvisation, musical cognitive science. Seminars and workshops, with a written mémoire at the centre; personal projects can feed the mémoire. M1 and M2 can each be spread over two years to combine with professional activity. Master Arts at Lille groups five arts (music, dance, theatre, cinema, visual arts).
entryRequirements: Bac+3 (licence). Musicology licence recommended. Selection: 'Étude de dossier'.
acceptsNonMusic: UNCLEAR — leaning NO. The page recommends a musicology licence and gives no statement admitting non-music backgrounds; I could not find a quote permitting them. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than a hard refusal. This is also a research/mémoire-centred master, not a production master — a poor fit for someone who wants to make records.
portfolioSpec: No portfolio. Dossier only: detailed curriculum documentation, licence transcripts, diplomas/certificates, lettre de motivation stating professional objectives, a ONE-PAGE research proposal (projet de recherche), CV, internship attestations if any.
auditionSpec: None. Quote: admission is by 'Étude de dossier' only — no audition, no épreuve.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED for 2027-28. Under décret n°2026-385, EUR 3,941/yr unless Lille exempts him.
totalCostEstimate: ~EUR 4,050/yr fees + Lille living (~EUR 750-900/month) => ~EUR 13,000-15,000/yr if not exempted.

languageRequirement: French; level not published on the page (UNVERIFIED) — B2/C1 expected.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: not published on the catalogue page. National monmaster.gouv.fr window is normally late February to late March. For him: Campus France Tunisie / Études en France procedure applies to him: platform opens 1 October 2026; master applications close approx. 15 January 2027 for September 2027 entry.

institution: Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès (UT2J) — ENSAV / ESAV, École Nationale Supérieure d'AudioVisuel
program: Master mention Cinéma et audiovisuel, parcours Son
accreditationStatus: Accredited university master delivered by ENSAV/ESAV, the audiovisual school inside UT2J. Sibling parcours in the same mention: Image, Réalisation, Production, Esthétique du cinéma, VFX/Architecture-Décor, Recherche Expérimentation (REX), Cinéma XR.
institutionType: (a) Public university — SUBJECT to décret n°2026-385 frais différenciés (master reference EUR 3,941/yr; exemptions capped at 25% of non-EU students in 2027-28).
whatYouStudy: Quoted content: 'prise de son. Montage son', 'traitement et mixage', 'diffusion', plus critical listening, acoustic fundamentals, and analogue and digital audio technology. This is the strongest pure studio-craft (Field B) programme found in this sweep at a French public university — it is film/audiovisual sound rather than electronic music composition, but it is the classical route into professional studio work.
entryRequirements: Quote: M1 requires 'un bac + 3 (180 ECTS)'; M2 requires 'un bac + 4 (240 ECTS)'. acceptsNonMusic: YES — and explicitly so for HIS degree. The accepted-backgrounds list names 'l'informatique' (computer science / IT) directly alongside the arts fields. auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — selection procedure not specified on the page. No live musical audition is implied by the programme's nature; expect dossier + possible entretien.

languageRequirement: French. Level not published (UNVERIFIED); Campus France Tunisie will require a French test (TCF/DELF), typically B2 minimum.

institution: INSAS — Institut National Supérieur des Arts du Spectacle et des Techniques de Diffusion
program: Master Radio Télévision Multimédia, spécialité Son (60 crédits)
qualification: Master (2e cycle) conferring the grade de master, Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. Quote of the cursus listing: 'RADIO TELEVISION MULTIMEDIA – spécialité Son (60 crédits)'. NOTE it is a 60-credit (one-year) master, not 120.
accreditationStatus: École supérieure des arts of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. INSAS also runs a 180-credit professional Bachelier Son.
institutionType: Belgian ESA (Wallonia-Brussels Federation). The French frais différenciés regime is irrelevant here.
whatYouStudy: Deepening of the concepts and practices of the sound professions developed in the first cycle — radio, television and multimedia sound. Documentary/fiction sound recording, post-production, sound direction. INSAS is a film-and-broadcast school, so this is Field B studio/location craft, not electronic-music composition.
entryRequirements: Quote of the general rule: access to the 2nd cycle 'est conditionné par l'avis de la commission d'admission qui statue au cas par cas sur la base du dossier administratif du candidat et de son parcours académique et/ou professionnel antérieur'. Holders of a first-cycle academic degree in the same programme awarded by the Communauté française have unconditional access. A prior enrolment for the admission examination is compulsory and passing it is required for any regular enrolment.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED but structurally UNLIKELY without prior sound training. The 60-credit master is explicitly framed as a deepening of what was 'développées au premier cycle' — i.e. it assumes the INSAS Bachelier Son or an equivalent. The commission decides case by case, which leaves a door open, but a BSc Software Engineering with no sound portfolio is a weak dossier here. No quote admitting non-specialists.

tuitionNonEU: WALLONIA + FRENCH-SPEAKING BRUSSELS (Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles), 2026-2027 — a single decree-set regime, identical at every institution. Droits d'inscription EUR 1,194 (published as 'montant à titre indicatif', subject to change by the Belgian government) PLUS a contribution supplémentaire (the successor to the old droit d'inscription spécifique / DIS) of EUR 4,175 per year = EUR 5,369/yr TOTAL. Legal basis: art. 105 §3bis of the décret du 7 novembre 2013 (décret paysage), as amended by the décret-programme du 11 décembre 2024. Transition: the EUR 4,175 already applies to ALL 2nd-cycle (master) students from 2026-2027, and to 1st-cycle students from 2027-2028 — so a master entrant in September 2027 pays it in full with no transitional relief. Payment schedule (ARTS² and INSAS publish the same shape): EUR 50 deposit by 15 Sept / 31 Oct 2026, balance of droits + the EUR 4,175 by 15 Jan / 1 Feb 2027. PER INSTITUTION: ARTS² Mons EUR 5,369; Conservatoire royal de Liège EUR 5,369; Conservatoire royal de Bruxelles EUR 5,369 (regime-wide figure — CRB's own fee page could not be reached, its published item is only 'La prochaine session des épreuves d'admission sera organisée entre le 23 août et le 9 septembre 2026'; the amount is decree-set and not institution-variable, but treat the CRB line as INSTITUTIONALLY UNVERIFIED); IAD Louvain-la-Neuve EUR 5,369 (published: 'minerval 1194 € par année académique' + '4175 €' payable by 31 January); INSAS Brussels EUR 5,369 (published payment plan: EUR 50 by 31/10/2026, EUR 4,125 balance by 01/02/2027). Means-tested reductions on the MINERVAL only (EUR 835 'condition intermédiaire', EUR 374 'condition modeste', EUR 0 boursier) do not reduce the EUR 4,175. FLANDERS, 2026-2027 — set per institution, and it exploded this year because the Flemish government removed non-EEA students from basic financing, forcing institutions to charge full cost. KASK & Conservatorium Gent (HoGent School of Arts): fixed EUR 916.20 + EUR 131.40 per credit = EUR 8,800.20 for a 60-credit model curriculum. Koninklijk Conservatorium Antwerpen (AP Hogeschool): 'Studiegeld buitenlandse studenten — Diploma- en creditcontracten: vast gedeelte 2500, variabel gedeelte per stp 375' = EUR 25,000 for 60 credits — by far the highest figure found anywhere in this sweep; plus EUR 65 opleidingsgebonden kosten for Muziek. Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel (Erasmushogeschool Brussel), artistic programmes: fixed EUR 1,181.40 + EUR 272 per credit = EUR 17,501.40 for 60 credits (up from about EUR 9,000, which triggered the 'Requiem for culture' student protest at the Queen Elisabeth Competition in May 2026; EhB decided on 28 April 2026 on a transitional measure that only partly offsets the rise for students ALREADY enrolled — a new 2027 entrant gets nothing from it). LUCA School of Arts (all campuses incl. Sint-Lukas Brussel and Lemmens Leuven), non-EEA enrolling from 2026-2027 onwards: fixed EUR 2,376.72 + EUR 118.62 per credit = EUR 9,823.92 for 60 credits, plus EUR 300 material cost per year. For comparison the Flemish standard (EEA) rate at LUCA in 2026-2027 is EUR 1,511.40.

scholarships: EXEMPTION QUESTION, SETTLED. In the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles the countries exempt from the EUR 4,175 contribution supplémentaire are fixed by ARES circulaire n°2026-001 du 12/02/2026 (which abrogates circulaire n°2025-01 du 18 février 2025 and applies from academic year 2026-2027). Its three annexes are: ANNEXE 1 'PAYS LES MOINS AVANCÉS (LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES)' — the UN LDC list, 44 countries: Afghanistan, Angola, Bangladesh, Bénin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodge, Comores, Djibouti, Érythrée, Éthiopie, Gambie, Guinée, Guinée-Bissau, Haïti, Kiribati, Laos, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritanie, Myanmar, Mozambique, Népal, Niger, Ouganda, République centrafricaine, RD Congo, Rwanda, Îles Salomon, Sénégal, Sierra Leone, Somalie, Soudan, Soudan du Sud, Tanzanie, Tchad, Timor oriental, Togo, Tuvalu, Yémen, Zambie. ANNEXE 2 'PAYS CLASSÉS AU BAS DE LA LISTE SUR L'INDICE DE DÉVELOPPEMENT HUMAIN' (ARES CA decision of 14 December 2021), 20 countries: Cameroun, Cap-Vert, Côte d'Ivoire, El Salvador, Ghana, Guatemala, Guinée équatoriale, Honduras, Kenya, Micronésie, Namibie, Nigeria, Pakistan, Palestine, Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée, République du Congo-Brazzaville, São Tomé-et-Príncipe, Syrie, Vanuatu, Zimbabwe. ANNEXE 3 'LISTE DE PAYS ADDITIONNELS' (ARES CA decision of 5 November 2024): Liban — one country only. TUNISIA APPEARS ON NONE OF THE THREE ANNEXES. He therefore gets NO exemption and pays the full EUR 5,369. Do not be misled by the fact that Tunisia IS one of the 32 ARES development-cooperation PARTNER COUNTRIES for scholarship purposes (alongside Morocco, Senegal, Vietnam, etc.) — the partner-country list and the fee-exemption annexes are different instruments. Other exemption routes that WOULD work: holding a Wallonie-Bruxelles International scholarship (a WBI bursary exempts him from the contribution supplémentaire as well as funding him — this is the single highest-value application he can make in Belgium); holding a Belgian secondary-education certificate from a French Community school after two years of schooling; enrolling in an AESS/teaching master; or qualifying as 'assimilé' under art. 3 §1 of the décret du 11 avril 2014 (long-term residence, refugee status, employment in Belgium, CPAS support, EU family member, long-term resident of another EU state). CAVEAT: circulaire 2026-001 states 'La présente circulaire est uniquement applicable aux universités' — a parallel instrument governs Hautes Écoles and Écoles supérieures des Arts, but IAD's own fee page confirms the ESA exemption categories are the same (LDC list, ARES list, French Community secondary diploma, 3rd cycle, initial teacher training, WBI bursary), and the statutory exemption in art. 105 §3bis is the UN LDC list, which excludes Tunisia either way. In Flanders, LUCA offers the Master Mind scholarship and EhB/RITCS + KC Brussel launched a crowdfunding campaign to retain international talent; amounts UNVERIFIED.
